target_customer: Teams building LLM agents, coding agents and RAG pipelines that pay per token
problem: Long contexts in agents and RAG inflate token costs and latency and can hurt accuracy. Compresr compresses context while keeping the details that matter to the query.
business_model: usage-based API plus open-source proxy (Context Gateway) and on-prem deployment

founders.name: Ivan Zakazov
education: EPFL, PhD researching LLM context compression

founders.name: Kamel Charaf
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page; title differs between listing and bio

competitors.name: LLMLingua-2 (Microsoft Research)
competitors.traction_then: Widely cited as the default production choice for token pruning
competitors.funding_then: Research project, not a venture company

technical_complexity.rationale: Question-aware compression models need research skill, and the CEO's PhD was on this topic, but the product is an API and proxy a small team can ship.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source alternatives such as LLMLingua exist and one commentary says the logic can be approximated with a cheap LLM. A third-party review disputed some benchmark claims.

incumbents: Model providers with prompt caching and native compaction
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know. The company is active as of the batch.

market_need_then: Agent token costs were rising as coding agents carried long histories, and Compresr's open-source Context Gateway proxy drew developer attention in early 2026 (reported 451 GitHub stars after about six weeks).

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and cost-focused imperative headlines such as stop paying for context your model does not need

branding.community_and_virality: Open-source Context Gateway repo got third-party write-ups and about 451 GitHub stars within six weeks of release.

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage with press on the product, nothing found about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Compresr is an active W26 company with no exit, shutdown or layoffs found. The CEO researched context compression in his PhD, giving founder market fit, and rising agent token costs give timing tailwind. Risks are open-source rivals and model providers building native compaction.
notes: Funding: an aggregator (Employbl, citing Diffbot) lists a $500K pre-seed with no investors, and Crunchbase lists pre-seed stage.
